title: The Three Payment Tools
moduleName: Payments: Simple Invoices, Products, and Payment Links
learningGoal: Understand the job of a product, invoice, and payment link before creating anything.

items.title: What is a Product?
items.description: A product is the saved record for something you sell. It can represent a physical item, digital item, session, package, ticket, programme, or service.

items.title: Product Record Includes
items.description: A name, a short description, a price, a payment type (one-time or recurring), and any tax or quantity settings that apply.

items.title: Important Note
items.description: Creating a product does not collect payment by itself. The product must be offered through an invoice, payment link, order form, store, calendar, or another supported checkout.

items.title: What is an Invoice?
items.description: An invoice is a payment request addressed to a named customer. It records what they are buying, the amount owed, the issue date, and the due date.

items.title: Use an Invoice When
items.description: The buyer is already known, the amount or scope is specific to that client, the buyer needs a formal record, payment is due by a particular date, you need to see status (draft, sent, viewed, paid, overdue).

items.title: What is a Payment Link?
items.description: A payment link is a shareable checkout page attached to one or more saved products and prices.

items.title: Use a Payment Link When
items.description: The offer and price are already set, several buyers may purchase the same offer, the buyer does not need a custom invoice first, you want to place the link in email, message, QR code, button, or social post.

items.title: Product
items.description: Stores what you sell and how it is priced. Example: 90-Minute Strategy Session.

items.title: Invoice
items.description: Requests payment from one named client. Example: Invoice Amy for a custom consulting session.

items.title: Payment Link
items.description: Gives buyers a reusable checkout. Example: Share a link for a workshop ticket.

keyPoint: Products store what you sell. Invoices request payment from named clients. Payment links provide reusable checkout pages. Choose the right tool for each situation.

actionSteps.title: Identify Your Offers
actionSteps.description: Write down 2-3 things you currently sell or plan to sell.

actionSteps.title: Choose the Right Tool
actionSteps.description: For each offer, decide: Is it a product? Would you use an invoice or payment link to sell it?

actionSteps.title: Write Down One Real Offer
actionSteps.description: Choose one offer you will use throughout this module.

nextLessonTitle: Prepare the Account and Plan the Sale

quizzes.question: What is the main job of a product in LeadProspectrr?

options.option_text: It stores what you sell and how it is priced
It automatically collects payments from customers
It sends invoices to all your contacts

quizzes.explanation: A product stores the name, description, price, and payment type for something you sell. It does not collect payment by itself—it must be offered through invoices, payment links, or other checkout methods.

quizzes.question: When should you use an invoice instead of a payment link?

options.option_text: When you want to share the same offer with many buyers
When the buyer is already known and the amount is specific to that client
When you want to post on social media
When you do not know who the buyer is

quizzes.explanation: Use an invoice when the buyer is known, the amount or scope is client-specific, they need a formal record, or payment is due by a specific date.

quizzes.question: What is a payment link best used for?

options.option_text: Sending custom billing records to one client
Creating a shareable checkout page for a fixed offer that many buyers can purchase

quizzes.explanation: A payment link creates a reusable checkout page for a fixed offer. It is ideal when several buyers may purchase the same thing and you want to share the link via email, social media, QR codes, or buttons.

title: Prepare the Account and Plan the Sale
moduleName: Payments: Simple Invoices, Products, and Payment Links
learningGoal: Check the payment foundation and define the offer before opening the product editor.

items.title: Go to Payments → Integrations
items.description: Confirm the payment provider intended for this account is connected.

items.title: What to Check
items.description: Correct business or sub-account connected, correct payment provider selected, test mode and live mode clearly identified, account can accept intended currency and payment method, you have permission to make payment changes.

items.title: Security Note
items.description: Do not enter private API keys or card details into training notes, screenshots, chat messages, or shared documents.

items.title: Go to Payments → Invoices & Estimates → Settings
items.description: Review general invoice details available in the account.

items.title: What to Review
items.description: Business name, address, contact email and phone, logo, default payment terms, invoice numbering or prefix, tax settings, accepted payment methods.

items.title: Tax Note
items.description: Tax rules vary by location and by what is being sold. Use advice from a qualified tax professional when unsure whether to charge tax.

items.title: Test Mode
items.description: Simulates payment and does not charge a real card.

items.title: Live Mode
items.description: Processes a real customer transaction.

items.title: Important
items.description: Provider settings for test and live mode may be separate. A working test connection does not prove live connection is ready. Do not test a live checkout with a customer's card.

items.title: C — Customer
items.description: Who is buying?

items.title: L — Label
items.description: Is the product name easy to understand?

items.title: E — Exact Amount
items.description: Is the price correct?

items.title: A — Arrangement
items.description: Is it one-time or recurring?

items.title: R — Result
items.description: What happens after payment?

keyPoint: Before creating products or payment links, check your payment provider connection, business details, and understand test vs live mode. Use the CLEAR check to plan your offer.

actionSteps.title: Check Payment Provider
actionSteps.description: Go to Payments → Integrations and verify everything is connected correctly.

actionSteps.title: Review Business Details
actionSteps.description: Go to Payments → Invoices & Estimates → Settings and confirm all details are accurate.

actionSteps.title: Complete CLEAR Check
actionSteps.description: Use the CLEAR framework to plan your offer before building.

quizzes.question: What should you check before creating products or payment links?

options.option_text: Payment provider connection, business details, and test vs live mode

quizzes.explanation: Before creating products, check your payment provider connection, business and invoice details, and understand the difference between test mode and live mode.

quizzes.question: What is the difference between test mode and live mode?

options.option_text: Test mode simulates payment without charging; live mode processes real transactions
Live mode is only for testing

quizzes.explanation: Test mode simulates payment without charging a real card. Live mode processes actual customer transactions. Always test in test mode first.

quizzes.question: What does the CLEAR offer check stand for?

options.option_text: Customer, Label, Exact amount, Arrangement, Result

quizzes.explanation: CLEAR stands for: Customer (who is buying), Label (is the name clear), Exact amount (is the price correct), Arrangement (one-time or recurring), Result (what happens after payment).

title: Create a Simple Product
moduleName: Payments: Simple Invoices, Products, and Payment Links
learningGoal: Create a reusable one-time service product with a clear name, description, and price.

items.title: Navigate to Products
items.description: Go to Payments → Products. Select Create Product. Choose the standard product option.

items.title: Name and Description
items.description: Name: 90-Minute Strategy Session. Description: A focused 90-minute session to review one business challenge and agree on the next actions.

items.title: Image (Optional)
items.description: Add an image only if it helps the buyer recognize the offer.

items.title: Keep Names Clear
items.description: Avoid internal codes or vague labels that a buyer will not understand.

items.title: Price Settings
items.description: Payment type: One-time. Amount: $495.00 (or your selected price). Currency: The currency used by the connected account.

items.title: Recurring Prices
items.description: Create recurring prices only after deciding billing frequency, start date, cancellation terms, and what the customer receives each period.

items.title: Optional Settings
items.description: Check taxes, product statement description, quantity, online-store visibility, inventory (if physical item).

items.title: Don't Enable Unnecessary Settings
items.description: Do not turn on a setting simply because it is available. It should match how this offer is sold and delivered.

items.title: Save and Inspect
items.description: Save the product, then reopen it and verify: name is correct, description is clear, amount and currency are correct, price is one-time, tax settings match, product is active.

items.title: Clear Names
items.description: Coach: Leadership Coaching Session — 60 Minutes. Consultant: Operations Review — Half Day. Speaker: Virtual Keynote — 45 Minutes.

items.title: Weak Names
items.description: Avoid vague names like: Coaching, Consulting Work, Speaking, Training, Plan A.

keyPoint: Create a clear, descriptive product with the correct price and payment type. Save and inspect before using it in invoices or payment links.

actionSteps.title: Create Your Product
actionSteps.description: Go to Payments → Products and create your service product with a clear name and description.

actionSteps.title: Set the Price
actionSteps.description: Add a one-time price with the correct amount and currency.

actionSteps.title: Save and Verify
actionSteps.description: Save the product, reopen it, and check all details are correct.

nextLessonTitle: Prepare and Send a Simple Invoice

quizzes.question: Why should a product be created before a payment link?

options.option_text: The payment link needs a saved product and price to display what the buyer is purchasing

quizzes.explanation: A payment link needs a saved product and price to display what the buyer is purchasing and how much they will pay. The product must exist first.

quizzes.question: What makes a good product name?

options.option_text: Clear, descriptive names buyers understand like 'Leadership Coaching Session — 60 Minutes'

quizzes.explanation: Good product names are clear and descriptive so buyers understand what they are purchasing. Avoid internal codes and vague labels.

quizzes.question: What should you check after saving a product?

options.option_text: Name, description, amount, currency, payment type, tax settings, and availability

quizzes.explanation: After saving, reopen the product and verify: name is correct, description is clear, amount and currency are correct, price is one-time (if intended), tax settings match, and product is active.

title: Prepare and Send a Simple Invoice
moduleName: Payments: Simple Invoices, Products, and Payment Links
learningGoal: Create a draft invoice for one named contact, inspect it, and understand the sending options.

items.title: Navigate to Invoices
items.description: Go to Payments → Invoices & Estimates. Select New → New Invoice.

items.title: Choose Test Contact
items.description: Select the test contact whose email address you control. Check their name, email, phone (if sending by text), and billing information.

items.title: Critical Check
items.description: An invoice sent to the wrong contact creates a privacy and payment problem. Stop and correct the record before sending.

items.title: Add Product
items.description: Add '90-Minute Strategy Session' from saved products. Confirm: Quantity is 1, Rate is correct, Tax is correct, Discount is correct (if agreed), Total matches agreement.

items.title: Review Details
items.description: Invoice number, Issue date, Due date, Payment terms, Notes or instructions, Accepted payment methods, Linked opportunity (if used).

items.title: Suggested Note
items.description: Thank you for choosing the 90-Minute Strategy Session. Payment confirms your session. Booking instructions will be sent after payment is recorded.

items.title: Important
items.description: Do not promise automatic delivery unless the follow-up process has been built and tested.

items.title: I — Identity
items.description: Is this the correct customer?

items.title: N — Number
items.description: Is the invoice number correct?

items.title: V — Value
items.description: Are subtotal, tax, discount, and total correct?

items.title: O — Offer
items.description: Is the product or service described clearly?

items.title: I — Important dates
items.description: Are issue date and due date correct?

items.title: C — Collection method
items.description: Can the customer use the intended payment method?

items.title: E — Email and experience
items.description: Is the sending address correct, and does the preview look professional?

items.title: Final Check
items.description: When every item passes, select Send and choose delivery method (email or text).

items.title: Training Safety
items.description: Send only to a test contact you control. Use test mode. Do not send practice invoices to real customers. Keep unfinished practice invoices in Draft.

keyPoint: Create invoices carefully, verify all details with the INVOICE check, and only send when everything is correct. Always double-check the recipient.

actionSteps.title: Create Draft Invoice
actionSteps.description: Go to Payments → Invoices & Estimates and create a new invoice for your test contact.

actionSteps.title: Add Product and Details
actionSteps.description: Add your saved product and set all invoice details correctly.

actionSteps.title: Run INVOICE Check
actionSteps.description: Verify Identity, Number, Value, Offer, Important dates, Collection method, Email and experience.

nextLessonTitle: Create and Share a Payment Link

quizzes.question: What should you check before sending an invoice?

options.option_text: Customer identity, invoice number, values, offer description, dates, payment method, and email experience

quizzes.explanation: Use the INVOICE check: Identity (correct customer), Number (correct invoice number), Value (subtotal, tax, discount, total), Offer (clear description), Important dates, Collection method, Email and experience.

quizzes.question: Why is it critical to verify the customer before sending an invoice?

options.option_text: It does not matter who receives it
An invoice sent to the wrong contact creates privacy and payment problems

quizzes.explanation: Sending an invoice to the wrong contact creates serious privacy issues and payment problems. Always verify the recipient before sending.

quizzes.question: What does the 'E' in INVOICE stand for?
quizzes.explanation: The E in INVOICE stands for Email and experience: Is the sending address correct, and does the preview look professional?

title: Create and Share a Payment Link
moduleName: Payments: Simple Invoices, Products, and Payment Links
learningGoal: Create a reusable checkout for the saved product and inspect it before sharing.

items.title: Navigate to Payment Links
items.description: Go to Payments → Payment Links. Select Create Link or Create New Payment Link.

items.title: Name Your Link
items.description: Enter a clear internal name, such as '90-Minute Strategy Session — $495'.

items.title: Select Product
items.description: Select '90-Minute Strategy Session'. Select the correct one-time price. Confirm currency and amount.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.description: If product or price does not appear, return to Payments → Products and check it was saved correctly and is available.

items.title: Available Options
items.description: Quantity, Adjustable quantity, Buyer contact fields, Coupon codes, Terms or consent checkboxes, Redirect or thank-you page, Product image and description, Payment methods, Branding or theme, Tracking details.

items.title: Keep It Simple
items.description: For the first payment link, keep the checkout short. Ask only for information needed to take payment and deliver the offer.

items.title: Save the Link
items.description: Select Save, then select Preview.

items.title: Preview Check
items.description: Open the checkout in a private browser window. Check it on phone-sized screen and desktop.

items.title: L — Label
items.description: Does the buyer see the correct offer name?

items.title: I — Information
items.description: Are the description and buyer fields clear?

items.title: N — Number
items.description: Are amount, currency, quantity, discount, and tax correct?

items.title: K — Keep going
items.description: Does the buyer know what happens after payment?

items.title: Copy the URL
items.description: Copy the checkout URL only after previewing and testing it.

items.title: Where to Share
items.description: Email, text message, website button, QR code, social message, proposal or follow-up document.

items.title: Reuse the Same Link
items.description: Use the same approved link rather than creating new links for every buyer when product and price are identical.

sections.title: When NOT to Use a Payment Link

items.title: Use Invoice Instead
items.description: Amount is different for each buyer, buyer needs purchase order first, offer contains private client-specific information, buyer negotiated different terms, link would expose offer that should not be public.

keyPoint: Create payment links with clear names, select the correct product and price, review settings, preview on desktop and mobile, use the LINK check, then share. Use invoices when payment links are not appropriate.

actionSteps.title: Create Payment Link
actionSteps.description: Go to Payments → Payment Links and create a new link with a clear name.

actionSteps.title: Select Product and Price
actionSteps.description: Choose your saved product and confirm the correct one-time price.

actionSteps.title: Preview and Test
actionSteps.description: Save, preview on desktop and mobile, run the LINK check before sharing.

quizzes.question: What does the LINK check stand for?
quizzes.explanation: LINK stands for: Label (correct offer name), Information (clear description and fields), Number (correct amount, currency, quantity), Keep going (buyer knows what happens after payment).

quizzes.question: When should you NOT use a general payment link?

options.option_text: When the offer and price are fixed
When the amount is different for each buyer or the offer contains private information
When you want to share on social media
When you have a saved product

quizzes.explanation: Do not use a general payment link when: amount varies per buyer, buyer needs PO first, offer has private info, terms were negotiated differently, or the link would expose a non-public offer. Use an invoice instead.

quizzes.question: Why preview the payment link on mobile?

options.option_text: Many buyers will complete purchases on mobile devices

quizzes.explanation: Many buyers complete purchases on mobile devices. Always preview your payment link on both desktop and mobile to ensure a good experience on all screen sizes.

title: Test the Full Payment Journey
moduleName: Payments: Simple Invoices, Products, and Payment Links
learningGoal: Run a controlled test and confirm the records, messages, checkout, and next action.

items.title: P — Product
items.description: Correct name, description, and price.

items.title: A — Account
items.description: Correct business, payment provider, and currency.

items.title: Y — Your buyer
items.description: Correct contact and delivery details.

items.title: F — Figures
items.description: Correct quantity, discount, tax, total, and due date.

items.title: I — Instructions
items.description: Clear note about what happens after payment.

items.title: R — Run a test
items.description: Use the approved test process.

items.title: S — Screen check
items.description: Review desktop and mobile checkout.

items.title: T — Track the result
items.description: Confirm payment and follow-up record inside LeadProspectrr.

items.title: Product Checklist
items.description: Reopen the product. Check name and description. Check one-time vs recurring. Check amount and currency. Check tax and availability settings.

items.title: Invoice Checklist
items.description: Use test contact you control. Confirm customer identity. Preview the invoice. Check dates, item, subtotal, tax, discount, total. Check email or text content. Confirm status changes as expected.

items.title: Link Checklist
items.description: Open in private browser. Check desktop and mobile layouts. Confirm offer name, amount, currency, quantity. Complete test-mode transaction. Check confirmation shown to buyer. Check payment/order record. Check contact record. Check receipt or notification. Check booking, delivery, or follow-up step.

items.title: Important
items.description: Test mode and live mode may use different provider settings. After test passes: confirm live provider connection separately, switch only intended checkout to live mode, open final live link without entering card details, check visible offer, amount, currency, and business details again.

keyPoint: Use the PAY FIRST safety check before any payment request goes live. Test products, invoices, and payment links thoroughly. Confirm test mode vs live mode settings.

actionSteps.title: Run PAY FIRST Check
actionSteps.description: Verify Product, Account, Your buyer, Figures, Instructions before testing.

actionSteps.title: Test Each Component
actionSteps.description: Test the product, invoice, and payment link using the checklists.

actionSteps.title: Confirm Live Mode
actionSteps.description: After test passes, verify live provider connection before going live.

nextLessonTitle: Apply the Payment Path to Your Business

quizzes.question: What does PAY FIRST stand for?

options.option_text: Pay All Your Fees Immediately, Receive Service Today
Product, Account, Your buyer, Figures, Instructions, Run a test, Screen check, Track the result
Purchase All Your Financial Items, Record Sales Transactions
Process All Yearly Financial Income Reports Swiftly Today

quizzes.explanation: PAY FIRST stands for: Product, Account, Your buyer, Figures, Instructions, Run a test, Screen check, Track the result. Use this before any payment request goes live.

quizzes.question: Why should you test in a private browser window?

options.option_text: It shows more closely what a buyer who is not signed in will see

quizzes.explanation: A private browser window shows what a buyer who is not signed into your account will see, giving you a more accurate test of the customer experience.

quizzes.question: What should you do after a test passes?

options.option_text: Immediately switch everything to live mode
Confirm the live provider connection separately before switching to live mode

quizzes.explanation: After a test passes, confirm the live provider connection separately. Test and live mode may use different provider settings. Switch only the intended checkout to live mode and verify again.

title: Apply the Payment Path to Your Business
moduleName: Payments: Simple Invoices, Products, and Payment Links
learningGoal: Build a payment path for a real offer used by your business.

items.title: Scenario A: Coach
items.description: Create one-time product for 60-minute coaching session. Prepare invoice for named client and payment link for same standard session.

items.title: Scenario B: Consultant
items.description: Create half-day review product. Use invoice for client-specific engagement. Decide if general payment link is appropriate.

items.title: Scenario C: Speaker
items.description: Create virtual keynote deposit product. Prepare invoice for event organizer. Do not create public link if amount varies by event.

items.title: Scenario D: Trainer
items.description: Create team workshop ticket product. Build reusable payment link for organizations purchasing same package at same price.

items.title: Scenario E: Service Business
items.description: Create initial service-call product. Prepare invoice for existing customer and link for fixed-price booking or deposit.

items.title: 1. Name Customer and Offer
items.description: Identify who is buying and what they are buying.

items.title: 2. Write Product Details
items.description: Product name and buyer-facing description.

items.title: 3. Set Price and Currency
items.description: Price, currency, and payment type (one-time).

items.title: 4. Decide on Tax/Discount
items.description: Whether tax, discount, or quantity applies.

items.title: 5. Create and Inspect Product
items.description: Build the product and verify all details.

items.title: 6. Create Draft Invoice
items.description: For a test contact.

items.title: 7. Create Payment Link
items.description: Only if offer and price can be shared safely.

items.title: 8. Run PAY FIRST Check
items.description: Verify everything before testing.

items.title: 9. Complete Test
items.description: Run approved test process.

items.title: 10. Record Next Action
items.description: What happens after payment and who owns it.

items.title: Complete When
items.description: One clearly named product with correct price and type. One invoice prepared for correct test contact. One payment link previewed on desktop and mobile (if appropriate). Correct provider and mode checked. Test result appears in payment and contact records. Buyer told what happens next. Named person owns delivery or follow-up.

items.title: Future Improvements
items.description: After basic payment path works, add one at a time: Recurring prices or subscriptions, Recurring invoices, Estimates, Deposits or payment schedules, Invoice reminders, Coupons, Multiple-product links, Text-to-pay, Payment-received workflows, Booking or digital delivery after payment, Pipeline updates and team notifications. Test complete buyer journey after every change.

keyPoint: Apply the payment path to your real business. Complete all exercise steps, reach the finish line, and test thoroughly. Add improvements one at a time after the basic path works.

actionSteps.title: Choose Your Scenario
actionSteps.description: Select the scenario closest to your business or create your own.

actionSteps.title: Work Through Exercise Steps
actionSteps.description: Complete all 10 steps from naming the customer to recording the next action.

actionSteps.title: Reach the Finish Line
actionSteps.description: Ensure all completion criteria are met before considering the payment path done.

quizzes.question: What is the first step in applying the payment path?

options.option_text: Name the customer and the offer

quizzes.explanation: The first step is to identify who is buying (the customer) and what they are buying (the offer). Planning before building prevents errors.

quizzes.question: When is the exercise complete?

options.option_text: When all criteria are met: product created, invoice prepared, link previewed, provider checked, test completed, and follow-up owner named
When you run out of time

quizzes.explanation: The exercise is complete when: product is clearly named with correct price, invoice prepared for correct contact, payment link previewed (if appropriate), provider and mode checked, test results appear in records, buyer knows next steps, and a named person owns follow-up.

quizzes.question: What should you do after the basic payment path works?

options.option_text: Add one improvement at a time and test the complete journey after every change

quizzes.explanation: After the basic payment path works, add improvements one at a time: recurring billing, estimates, deposits, reminders, coupons, workflows, etc. Test the complete buyer journey after every change.
